medicaid_quality_cms.description: Annual state-level performance data on the Medicaid and CHIP Adult Core Set and Child Core Set quality measures, as voluntarily reported by states to CMS and analyzed by Mathematica via the Quality Measure Reporting (QMR) system. Measures span behavioral health (e.g., follow-up after ED visits for mental illness, substance use disorder treatment), primary and preventive care (e.g., well-child visits, immunizations), maternal and perinatal health (e.g., prenatal and postpartum care, low birthweight), dental health, care of chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, asthma, hypertension), and long-term services and supports. Each annual dataset includes state rates and national 25th and 75th percentile benchmarks. Data cover federal fiscal years 2014–2023. Reporting is voluntary; not all states report all measures each year. The wide-format standard file contains one row per state-year-payer-domain combination, with each measure-statistic combination as a separate column following the naming convention medicaid_{measure_abbr}_{population}_{sub_metric}_{stat} where population is 'ch' (child) or 'ad' (adult), sub_metric captures time windows or sub-components, and stat is 'rate', 'pct_25', or 'pct_75'.
medicaid_quality_cms.restrictions: Public domain. CMS/Medicaid.gov data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nis.name: National Immunization Survey-Teen (NIS-Teen)
nis.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nis.location: Vaccination Coverage among Adolescents (13-17 Years), TeenVaxView
nis.description: The National Immunization Surveys (NIS) are a group of telephone surveys used to monitor vaccination coverage among children 19-35 months, teens 13-17 years, flu vaccinations for children 6 months-17 years, and COVID-19 vaccination for children, teens, and adults. The surveys are sponsored and conducted by the National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases (NCIRD) of the CDC and authorized by the Public Health Service Act. NIS provides population-based, state and local area estimates of vaccination coverage using a standard survey methodology. Surveys collect data through telephone interviews with parents or guardians in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and some U.S. territories. Cell phone numbers are randomly selected and called to enroll age-eligible children. With parental permission, vaccination providers are contacted to verify immunization records. NIS-Teen covers adolescents aged 13-17 and reports coverage for HPV, Tdap, MenACWY, MMR, hepatitis A and B, and varicella by survey year for states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands, plus pooled 2018-2022 estimates by insurance, poverty, race and ethnicity, and urbanicity. HHS regions and sub-state local areas published by CDC are not included here.
nis.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

school_immunizations.name: PopHIVE school immunization assessments
school_immunizations.organization: PopHIVE, Yale School of Public Health
school_immunizations.location: Per-state standard files and source notes
school_immunizations.description: State health departments publish the results of their annual school-entry immunization assessments in different formats (open data portals, workbooks, PDF reports, registry reports). The PopHIVE school_immunizations repository ingests each state into a wide standard file keyed by school year, county, and grade. This source takes the states that publish adolescent-grade (6th or 7th grade, or a registry adolescent series) Tdap, MenACWY, or HPV coverage, keeps their county and state rows, and maps each state's columns onto a common set. Coverage definitions, the grade assessed, and denominators vary by state; compare within a state over time rather than across states. Connecticut reports by county through 2023-24 and by planning region from 2024-25. Washington assessed 6th grade through 2019-20 and 7th grade from 2020-21.
school_immunizations.restrictions: Public data published by the state agencies; no access restrictions. Cite the state source for a given state.

nnds.name: National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS)
nnds.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nnds.description: The National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) is a nationwide collaboration that enables all levels of public health to share notifiable disease related health information. Public health uses this information to monitor, control, and prevent the occurrence and spread of state-reportable and nationally notifiable infectious and some non-infectious diseases and conditions. NNDSS publishes weekly cumulative year-to-date counts; this bundle differences consecutive weeks within each MMWR year to get weekly counts for pertussis, meningococcal disease (all serogroups, serogroups ACWY, and serogroup B), tetanus, mumps, varicella, and acute hepatitis B. Negative values are downward revisions by CDC. Missing values are stored as zero in the source, so measure-years with no national reporting are omitted.
nnds.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
